An independent project by one person. A password manager that needs only your file: no account, no server, no tracking.
Your passwords live in a standard KeePass file that stays where you put it. The same file opens in KeePassXC, KeePassDX and other KeePass apps.
One library written in Rust. It does everything that touches your secrets, and both apps use the same one.

The apps only draw screens and talk to the system. Security-critical work is the same code on Android and iOS, so a vault behaves identically everywhere and is checked once. Rust rules out whole classes of memory bugs, and secrets are wiped as soon as they are no longer needed.
No network code, no analytics, no accounts. It never writes your master password, keys or decrypted data to disk. Only the encrypted file you chose is saved.

Create one, or open a KeePass file

Vazie Keep keeps your passwords in an ordinary KeePass file (.kdbx). No account is needed.

If you have no vault yet, tap Create vault: choose a name and a master password, then where to save the file. You can add a key file too — then unlocking needs both the password and the file.

If you already have a vault — from KeePassXC or KeePassDX, say — open its file: the app works with it where it is.

A master password cannot be recovered. Write it down and keep it somewhere safe, and keep a key file apart from the vault, with a backup.
Through a cloud drive, not Vazie\'s servers

Vazie has no cloud for your vaults: the file stays where you keep it.

To use one vault on your phone and your computer, put the .kdbx file in a cloud drive both devices have (Google Drive, Dropbox or Yandex Disk, for example) and open it in Vazie Keep through the system file picker.

Changes are saved back into the same file. If the file was changed on another device in the meantime, Vazie Keep won't silently overwrite those changes or lose yours.

On a computer the same file opens in KeePassXC or any other KeePass app.
Fill passwords in apps and Chrome

Open Settings → AutoFill and choose Vazie Keep as the AutoFill service. Matching entries then appear on sign-in forms; you confirm the choice with your fingerprint or master password, and only the chosen entry is revealed.

Turn on Offer to save passwords so Android offers to save a new password to your vault after you sign in or sign up. Your vault doesn't change without your confirmation.

On Android 14 and later, Vazie Keep can hold passkeys. Tap Passkeys in Settings and turn Vazie Keep on in the system list. Passkeys are stored in your vault file.
Open your vault without typing the master password

Unlock your vault with its master password first, then turn on Biometric unlock in Settings. From then on you can open it with your fingerprint or another strong method set up on the phone.

The master password keeps working. If the vault has a key file, you still need it every time.

If you change the fingerprints in your phone's settings, turn biometric unlock on again.

Export your passwords from the old app, open your vault in Vazie Keep and choose Import from another app in the menu.

CSV files with a header row (browsers, KeePassXC, LastPass and the like), 1Password (.1pux and CSV) and Bitwarden (JSON and CSV) work. Encrypted exports aren't supported.

Entries are added to the open vault, folders become groups, and nothing is replaced. Attachments aren't imported.

Delete the export file afterwards: it holds your passwords in plain text.

Everything that protects your passwords is free and needs no account: vaults, master passwords, key files, biometrics, AutoFill, passkeys, the password generator and import. The free version is not a trial and isn't limited over time.

Keep+ adds: several vaults and switching between them, one-time codes (TOTP), an entry's history of changes, and adding attachments.

Keep+ belongs to your Vazie Account, not to a device. If it ends, every vault stays with you: you can open and read them all, and edit your main one.
